---
title: "Extensions"
---

qmd-fast keeps a lean core and pushes power to **extensions**. An extension is a
folder under `_extensions/<name>/` with an `_extension.yml` manifest plus whatever
CSS, JS, and templates it ships. There are three things an extension can do, from
simplest to most powerful: contribute a **format/theme**, declare
**shortcodes**, and register a client-side **enhancer**.

## Format & theme extensions

A format extension is selected by name in the front matter:

```yaml
format:
  liquid-glass-revealjs:   # <name>-<base>, base is revealjs or html
    slide-number: true
```

Its `_extensions/liquid-glass/_extension.yml` contributes includes, a theme, and
resources to the matching base format:

```yaml
contributes:
  formats:
    revealjs:
      theme: [dark, liquid-glass.css]      # .css layers inlined ahead of the deck
      format-resources: [liquid-glass.js]  # copied next to the output / served in preview
      include-in-header:  [{ file: head.html }]
      include-after-body: [{ file: init.html }]
```

The contributed markup is injected **before** the document's own front-matter
`include-*`, so your page can still override the extension. `format-resources` are
copied next to the built page (and resolved by bare name in the live preview), so
an injected `<script src="liquid-glass.js">` works in both.

## Declarative shortcodes

A shortcode is a `{{< name args >}}` tag in the body that expands to an HTML
template — perfect for embeds, with no JavaScript. Declare them under
`contributes.shortcodes` as a name → template map:

```yaml
contributes:
  shortcodes:
    youtube: '<div class="ratio"><iframe src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/{{1}}" allowfullscreen></iframe></div>'
    callout: '<aside class="note"><strong>{{title}}</strong> {{body}}</aside>'
```

Then in any document that activates the extension:

```markdown
{{< youtube dQw4w9WgXcQ >}}
{{< callout title="Heads up" body="this expanded from a shortcode" >}}
```

Positional args fill `{{1}}`, `{{2}}`, …; named `key=value` args (quotes group
spaces) fill `{{key}}`. Expansion is line-preserving, so click-to-source still
points at the right line. Unknown `{{< … >}}` tags are left untouched.

## Client enhancers

For anything interactive, ship a `.js` file (via `format-resources` or an
`include-after-body`) that registers an **enhancer** through the public API:

```js
window.qmdEnhancers.register(function (root) {
  root.querySelectorAll('.timestamp:not([data-done])').forEach(function (el) {
    el.dataset.done = '1';
    el.textContent = new Date(el.dataset.epoch * 1000).toLocaleString();
  });
});
```

A registered `fn(root)` runs after every (re)mount in the live preview, on load in
the static build, and once immediately if it registers after the page is already
mounted. Make it **idempotent** (guard with a data-attribute), since it re-runs on
every change. This is the same registry the built-in copy buttons and mermaid use,
so a third-party enhancer is indistinguishable from core's.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Diagnostics, not silence

A typo'd extension name, a malformed `_extension.yml`, or a missing
`contributes.formats.<base>` block is reported in the dev menu and the build log —
so a broken extension never fails silently.
:::
